lens: FINDINGS ANSWERED AND FAIRNESS: whether the 24 first-round findings are answered where A7 says, whether A5's points are faithful to PROTOCOL.md sections 5, 8, 9 and 10 and show the owner real alternatives and consequences, whether anything new in the second version is wrong, overstated, softened or misattributed (including the lead's note), plus privacy and format.

findings.where: Lead's note, lines 6-7 ("A1 in the lead's addendum lists each one that the final run, the three skeptics or the two report checkers found wrong or too wide"). Reconciler's text, line 59 ("its runs from 18:34:26 to 18:46:03"), line 355 ("The full B1 tables, with every interval, are in V\reconcile\work\tables.md") and line 389 ("tables.md (the main row and B1 tables)"). A1, lines 403-488.
findings.what: The second version's A1 dropped two corrections that the first version's A1 made (its items 1 and 2), and both had been verified. So two wrong statements in the reconciler's text are uncorrected again, and the note's claim that A1 lists every such statement is false. (i) Section 1 says reconcile.py re-read the compare files up to 18:46:03; the reads went on to 18:49:41. (ii) Sections 6 and 7 point the reader to work\tables.md for "the full B1 tables, with every interval", and that file was never written. A7 cannot show these two, because neither checker raised them as findings: both confirmed the first version's corrections.
findings.evidence: report.md.before_fix1 lines 399-403 hold the dropped items: "the runs of reconcile.py re-read the compare files from 18:34:26 to 18:49:41 ..., not to 18:46:03" and "work\tables.md was not written; work\r30_tables.py prints its tables and keeps no file". work\opened_official.jsonl: the 360 'reconcile.py' entries run from 18:34:26 to 18:49:41, and the 16 'bytes' entries from 18:43:43 to 18:49:41 (my k06). V\reconcile\work holds no tables.md. check_facts.json 'checked': "reconcile.py: 360 opens, 18:34:26 to 18:49:41 ... A1 item 1 is right" and "work\tables.md is absent". A search of the second version finds no '18:49:41' and no tables.md correction (k02).
findings.fix: Restore both as A1 items. (1) "Section 1: reconcile.py's runs re-read the compare files from 18:34:26 to 18:49:41 (360 opens, plus 16 byte reads of pairs.parquet), not to 18:46:03." (2) "Sections 6 and 7: work\tables.md was not written (r30_tables.py only prints). The B1 tables are in A6, and every B1 number with its interval is in A's and B's results.json under b1." The note's "lists each one" then holds.

findings.what: The report puts the lead's comparison "in code" in place of the asserts the reconcile skeptic asked for, but no saved code does it. The addendum lists four lead scripts (lines 399-400), and none of them compares A's and B's B1 status, run or identity records. findings.evidence: V\_lead\scripts holds only recover_writes.py, tally.py (group status tallies and test_set entries), scan_shap_mtimes.py and b1_tables.py (A against B on pair statistics, families, own-history share, top 3 and top 10 only). My k04 on work\summary.json b1, all five problems: A_status = B_status, A_registered = B_registered, A_meta_equal = B_meta_equal, A_run = B_run and A_identity = B_identity. identity_reconciler: max diff 0.0 over 309,000 and 121,000 values. The completeness checker's fix asked to "say how the equality was checked".
findings.fix: Save the comparison script and its output in V\_lead\scripts and name it in the addendum. Otherwise, say that the equality was confirmed by the reconcile skeptic (by hand) and by both report checkers, and drop "stands in their place".

findings.where: A4, the numbers, item 1 (lines 563-580), text new in the second version
findings.what: Two statements go beyond the s41 output they cite. (i) "No pair without BARDL ... has ... a collation dependence above 1e-12": in s41, every pair without BARDL has an RBO spread above 1e-12, up to 2.3e-5. (ii) The list of BARDL cells that "depend on that rule" reads as complete but is a selection. All eight BARDL pair-levels move, and some unlisted cells move as much as listed ones.
findings.evidence: s41_tie_artifacts.json (my k07, k08). All 22 pairs without BARDL have an RBO p 0.95 spread above 1e-12, and 18 also at p 0.9. The largest is fire, variable level, rival_lgbm|rival_lgbm_tweedie: RBO p 0.95 0.60137 against 0.60140, a spread of 2.25e-5. pm25 variable rival_lgbm|treeroute: 6.6e-6. Jaccard and top-20-union Spearman spreads are 0 there, and no pair without BARDL has a tie-only member. Unlisted BARDL moves: variable-level bardl|ridge (RBO p 0.9 0.055 vs 0.101; p 0.95 0.152 vs 0.234; Jaccard top 10 0 vs 0.053; top-20-union Spearman 0.033 vs -0.037); variable bardl|lgbm RBO p 0.95 0.253 vs 0.328; variable bardl|rf RBO p 0.9 0.153 vs 0.197; feature bardl|treeroute RBO p 0.95 0.242 to 0.277. skeptic_numbers.json finding 1 has the same 1e-12 sentence, so the report copied an error that its cited source contradicts.
findings.fix: Write: "no pair without BARDL has a tie-only top-k member; there the collation moves only RBO, by at most 2.3e-5, below the printed precision". Mark the BARDL list as examples, and let A5 point 3's footnote cover every BARDL pair at both levels.

findings.where: A5 point 3, line 636 (the proposed footnote text)
findings.what: "BARDL gives 0 to 93 of its 96 variables" is wrong. BARDL has three variables (nine columns); 96 is the size of NDVI's variable-level J. If this footnote text were adopted, it would contradict section 10.
findings.evidence: PROTOCOL.md section 10 lines 618-623 ("beyond its three variables at the variable level, and beyond its nine columns") and section 5 lines 403-405. A4 item 1, line 563, says it correctly: "93 of the 96 variables of J".
findings.fix: "BARDL gives exactly 0 to 93 of the 96 variables of J (it reads three variables, nine columns)".

findings.what: Three gaps. (1) Route (a) names its disclosure and consequence for S3.13 only. Under (a), the main-text table's fire row would also print treeroute's top 3 and own-history share [CI], which AW4_main_row.json and AW4_table.md lack. The first version said "S3.13 and the main row ... say so". (2) "rest on few finite draws" fits 64 of 2,000, not 1,140 or 1,380. (3) The C21 parenthetical says compare_shap "made no choice there". Its percentile helper, which gives every other official interval, returns an interval from one finite replicate on. That is the rule the proposal follows, and it supports the proposal.
findings.evidence: PROTOCOL.md section 10 line 552 (the main-text table) and section 9 lines 540-542. report.md.before_fix1 line 529. My k03: n_finite 64, 1,140 and 1,380, all [0, 1]; no other problem has an interval between 1 and 1,999. shapv1_stats.py percentile_ci (lines 259-266) gives NaN only when no value is finite, and is used at compare_shap.py lines 235, 243-244, 291 and 376. In the official pairs.parquet, every statistic has 2,000 finite except the sign agreement, which has 0 (k05).
findings.fix: In (a), add the note under the main-text table, and say that its fire row then differs from AW4_main_row.json. Write "on fewer than 2,000 finite draws (64, 1,140 and 1,380)". State that compare_shap's percentile helper gives an interval for any number of finite replicates.

findings.what: "C10, still open" labels an owner question with the same name as the spec's open choice C10 (ties and collation). findings.what: "S3.13 will show intervals on B1's shares" is true for B1's per-player shares and family shares, not for its top-10 shares. Section 10 gives B1 "none for the top-k lists", and A6 prints B1's top 10 without intervals. So the consequences are: under (a), only the family shares are treated differently from B1; under (b), the main models' top-10 shares would carry intervals that B1's do not.
findings.evidence: PROTOCOL.md section 10 lines 597-599. A6 lines 718 and 733 ("no interval for a top-k list"). The A6 family-share table has intervals (lines 708-715).
findings.fix: State both consequences: (a) leaves the family shares asymmetric; (b) makes the top-10 shares asymmetric the other way.
